deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. The upper part of the sheet is a fair copy, in Riemann's hand (attributed by the folio's provenance), of two German epigrams in elegiac/hexameter form, each signed 'Klopstock'. The rest of the folio is blank apart from archival foliation (185, and an older 188).

Epigram 1 is on teaching versus books. If a teacher presents knowledge without living grace (lebende Anmuth), the youth turns to the book and learns faster and better there, because he learns by himself. Yet no book can displace the experienced teacher whose eloquence inspires the inquiring youth. That teacher prepares before going onto the stage (Schauplatz) and has often read two hours in order to teach one.

Epigram 2 is on the reception of new ideas. If you say something new, say it as precisely as possible, but be fully certain that people will see it askew and explain you falsely. For the idea commits, after all, the 'terrible fault of novelty', and no denial (or demonstration) is enough once one shows it.

The page belongs to the 'Naturphilosophie' bundle as a personal note or excerpt. It is presumably a pedagogical and epistemological maxim Riemann found congenial, perhaps connected with his own lecturing and with the reception of his novel ideas. There are no derivations to reconstruct.

results.what: Copied Klopstock epigrams on teaching (teacher vs. book) and on the reception of novel ideas

deep.surprise_reason: Non-mathematical page: a copied pair of Klopstock epigrams. Of mild biographical interest for Riemann's attitude to teaching and to novelty, but contains no scientific content.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Wem[?]' should read 'Wenn die Wissenschaft lehrt'. 'lebender Anmuth' is confirmed.
Line 3: the reading 'Schneller lernt er sie dort, und besser, weil er sie selbst lernt' looks correct.
Line 6: 'eh'[?], wer[?] gesellt[?] auf den Schauplatz' is probably 'eh' er geht auf den Schauplatz'.
Line 7: the first word 'Leicht[?]' is uncertain, possibly 'Meist' or 'Dieß'. The line otherwise reads 'hat er oft zwei Stunden gelesen, um eine zu lehren'.
Second epigram, line 1: probably 'Sagst du Neues, so sag's so bestimmt als möglich; doch sei auch', rather than 'Wenn man Neues dir sagt, so bestimmt es möglich'.
Second epigram, line 2: probably 'Völlig gewiß, man sieht's schief, und erklärt dich falsch'.
Second epigram, line 3: 'begehrt' should be 'begeht ja nun einmal den schrecklichen Fehler der Neuheit'.
Second epigram, line 4: 'dann' should be 'wenn/denn'. The last word 'gemacht' is doubtful, possibly 'genug'.
